summary_1line: Bhishma recounts Yama’s teaching that gifts of sesame, water, lamps, gems, and robes bring great merit and benefit ancestors and the giver.

image_candidates.scene_text: Yama, lord of the dead, rises from his throne to respectfully worship the mistakenly brought Brahmana in his dark hall.
A fearsome messenger of Yama with crow-like features and blood-red eyes seizes a Brahmana in the peaceful town of Parnasala.
Pilgrims drink at a roadside water shelter with lamps glowing in the dusk, symbolizing charitable gifts praised by Yama.
